name: Video Game History
description: Explore video game history, from early arcade hits and home consoles to influential designers, PC milestones, and independent games.

questions.question: Which 1972 Atari arcade game became an early commercial hit by simulating table tennis?
questions.explanation_correct: Pong was a simple table tennis simulator that sparked the arcade and home console boom of the 1970s.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Space Invaders and Pac-Man debuted in the late 70s and early 80s, and Asteroids in 1979.

questions.question: Which Japanese company released the arcade game Space Invaders in 1978?
questions.explanation_correct: Tomohiro Nishikado designed Space Invaders for Taito; the game became a major arcade success.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nintendo found success later with Donkey Kong, Sega produced other arcade games, and Namco published Pac-Man.

questions.question: What was Pac-Man originally going to be called, inspired by the Japanese phrase for mouth-snapping sounds?
questions.explanation_correct: The title was changed to Pac-Man before its US release due to concerns that vandals would deface the 'P' to make an 'F'.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Munch, Chomp, and Gobble are English words describing eating, but none were the original Japanese name.

questions.question: Which home console released in the late 1970s popularized interchangeable cartridges instead of built-in games?
questions.explanation_correct: The Atari VCS (later known as the 2600) achieved massive success and defined the home entertainment market for years.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Magnavox Odyssey was the first home console, while ColecoVision and Intellivision were later competitors.

questions.question: Which legendary designer created Mario, Donkey Kong, and The Legend of Zelda for Nintendo?
questions.explanation_correct: Miyamoto was a key designer on Donkey Kong, Mario, and The Legend of Zelda, working with other Nintendo developers including Takashi Tezuka.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hideo Kojima created Metal Gear, Yu Suzuki designed Sega arcade hits, and Akira Toriyama was a manga artist and Dragon Quest designer.

questions.question: Which development studio revolutionized the first-person shooter genre by releasing Wolfenstein 3D and Doom in the early 1990s?
questions.explanation_correct: id Software, led by John Carmack and John Romero, created the 3D engines that defined the modern FPS genre.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Epic Games created Unreal, Valve released Half-Life in the late 90s, and 3D Realms was known for Duke Nukem.

questions.question: What name was given to the protagonist of the 1981 arcade game Donkey Kong before he was named Mario?
questions.explanation_correct: In Donkey Kong, the player character was a carpenter named Jumpman who rescued his girlfriend Pauline.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Plumber was his later occupation, Mr. Video was Miyamoto's concept name, and Ossan is a Japanese colloquial term for 'middle-aged guy'.

questions.question: In which year did Nintendo launch the NES in a limited North American test market?
questions.explanation_correct: Nintendo launched the NES in a New York test market in 1985 and expanded its release afterward. It helped revive the North American console market after the 1983 crash.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The crash began in 1983, the NES was widely distributed by 1987, and the Game Boy was released in 1989.

questions.question: Which Soviet programmer created Tetris in 1984 while working at the Academy of Sciences of the USSR?
questions.explanation_correct: Pajitnov wrote Tetris on an Electronika 60 computer, drawing inspiration from pentomino puzzle games.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brin co-founded Google, Kaspersky created antivirus software, and Sergeev is not associated with Tetris.

questions.question: Which 1997 RPG published by Interplay launched a post-apocalyptic franchise with a retro-futuristic style?
questions.explanation_correct: Fallout utilized the S.P.E.C.I.A.L. character system and served as the spiritual successor to the 1988 game Wasteland.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Wasteland was the predecessor, Diablo is Blizzard's action RPG hack'n'slash, and Baldur's Gate is a D&D-based RPG.

questions.question: Which 1983 LaserDisc arcade game features the knight Dirk the Daring and hand-drawn animation by Don Bluth?
questions.explanation_correct: Dragon's Lair featured hand-drawn animation by Don Bluth, a former Disney animator, and captivated players with its movie-like quality.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Space Ace and Cliff Hanger also used LaserDisc animation, while M.A.C.H. 3 combined LaserDisc footage with shooter gameplay.

questions.question: Who was Sega's blue mascot created in the early 1990s to compete with Nintendo's Mario?
questions.explanation_correct: Sonic the Hedgehog debuted in 1991 on the Sega Genesis (Mega Drive) to show off the console's high-speed processing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Alex Kidd was Sega's mascot in the 80s, Ristar starred in a 1995 platformer, and Opa-Opa is from Fantasy Zone.

questions.question: Which life simulation game designed by Will Wright and developed by Maxis was released in 2000 and became a major PC hit?
questions.explanation_correct: Maxis developed The Sims and Electronic Arts published it. Players guide the daily activities of simulated characters.
questions.explanation_incorrect: SimCity is a city builder, Spore deals with evolution, and Second Life is a virtual online world.

questions.question: Who is the creator of the acclaimed Metal Gear series and a pioneer of cinematic storytelling in video games?
questions.explanation_correct: Kojima directed the original Metal Gear for the MSX2 computer in 1987, pioneering stealth gameplay over direct action.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mikami created Resident Evil, Kamiya directed Devil May Cry and Bayonetta, and Nomura designed characters for Final Fantasy.

questions.question: Which of the original Pac-Man ghosts is pink in its standard appearance?
questions.explanation_correct: Pinky is the pink ghost in the original game; its behavior differs from that of the other three ghosts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Blinky is red, Inky is cyan, and Clyde is orange in their standard appearances.

questions.question: Which Sony console released in Japan in late 1994 popularized 3D graphics and the CD-ROM format?
questions.explanation_correct: The Sony PlayStation won the fifth-generation console war due to its developer-friendly architecture and CD format.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The PlayStation 2 launched in 2000, the Sega Saturn was its 1994 rival, and the Nintendo 64 used cartridges.

questions.question: Which real-time strategy (RTS) game released by Blizzard Entertainment in 1998 became a national e-sport phenomenon in South Korea?
questions.explanation_correct: StarCraft, along with its expansion Brood War, laid the foundations for professional gaming and televised e-sports leagues.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Warcraft II and C&C were earlier RTS hits, and Age of Empires focused on human history.

questions.question: Which Swedish programmer created Minecraft under the Mojang banner before selling the studio to Microsoft in 2014?
questions.explanation_correct: Markus 'Notch' Persson created the initial versions of Minecraft in 2009 as an independent sandbox project.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bergensten took over as lead designer, Andersson led Paradox development, and Fares directed co-op games like It Takes Two.

questions.question: Which 1982 arcade game challenges players to change the colors of cubes by hopping around an isometric pyramid?
questions.explanation_correct: In Q*bert, players changed the colors of cubes on a pyramid while avoiding enemies like Coily the snake.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Zaxxon was an isometric space shooter, Marble Madness involved rolling a trackball, and Paperboy was a newspaper delivery game.

questions.question: Which 1989 Nintendo handheld was bundled with Tetris in North America?
questions.explanation_correct: The North American Game Boy bundle included Tetris. Bundle contents differed between markets and releases.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Game Gear and Atari Lynx were competing handhelds; Game Boy Color was released later.

questions.question: Which 1993 adventure game created by brothers Rand and Robyn Miller became a major PC hit with its mysterious island and pre-rendered worlds?
questions.explanation_correct: Myst featured immersive pre-rendered 3D graphics and atmospheric sound, serving as a primary system seller for CD-ROM drives.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Riven was the 1997 sequel to Myst, and Monkey Island and Grim Fandango were LucasArts point-and-click titles.

questions.question: Which American game designer co-founded Firaxis Games and created the landmark turn-based strategy franchise Civilization?
questions.explanation_correct: Sid Meier authored multiple seminal strategy and simulation titles, and his name became a recognizable quality brand.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Molyneux created Populous and Fable, Garriott created Ultima, and Spector directed Deus Ex.

questions.question: Which home console was the last system manufactured by Sega, featuring a built-in modem and memory cards with screens (VMU)?
questions.explanation_correct: The Sega Dreamcast debuted in 1998 in Japan and 1999 in the West, but struggled to compete against the hyped PlayStation 2.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Saturn was its predecessor, Sega CD was a Genesis add-on, and the Genesis was Sega's 16-bit console.

questions.question: Which 1998 FPS developed by Valve integrated much of its storytelling into first-person gameplay rather than relying on traditional cutscenes?
questions.explanation_correct: Players controlled scientist Gordon Freeman, experiencing the Black Mesa facility disaster entirely from a first-person perspective.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Quake II and Unreal are earlier shooters, while Deus Ex is a hybrid RPG/FPS released in 2000.

questions.question: Which French designer created the 1991 cinematic platformer Another World, doing the programming, art, and rotoscoped animations himself?
questions.explanation_correct: Chahi utilized vector graphics to create smooth rotoscoped animations and a cinematic feel without dialog.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Raynal created Alone in the Dark, Ancel created Rayman, and Cage created Heavy Rain.

questions.question: Which coin-operated Spacewar! adaptation was installed at Stanford University in 1971?
questions.explanation_correct: Galaxy Game adapted Spacewar! on a PDP-11 and was installed at Stanford in 1971. Computer Space also appeared as a coin-operated video game that year.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Computer Space was Nolan Bushnell's commercial arcade game, Spacewar! was the non-commercial university game, and Space Travel was a Unix game.

questions.question: Which 1996 Nintendo console had a controller with a central analog control stick and later supported the optional Rumble Pak?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nintendo 64 controller included a control stick. The Rumble Pak was a separate accessory introduced in 1997, not a built-in feature.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The SNES was a 16-bit console, the GameCube was the N64's successor, and the Virtual Boy was a failed 3D headset.

questions.question: Which 1992 real-time strategy game developed by Westwood Studios established the classic RTS design template?
questions.explanation_correct: Dune II introduced harvesting resources, base construction, and selecting and commanding units via a mouse.
questions.explanation_incorrect: C&C and Warcraft were developed later, heavily inspired by Dune II. Herzog Zwei was an early Genesis strategy game.

questions.question: Which 2008 independent platformer created by Jonathan Blow helped kickstart the modern indie game boom with time-manipulation mechanics?
questions.explanation_correct: Braid was a massive critical and commercial success on Xbox Live Arcade, showing that small indie games could compete with AAA titles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Super Meat Boy, Fez, and Limbo were also major indie hits of the era but were released slightly later.

questions.question: Which British programmer co-created the open-ended space trading and combat simulator Elite in 1984?
questions.explanation_correct: David Braben and Ian Bell designed Elite for the BBC Micro, featuring a wireframe 3D procedural universe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chris Roberts created Wing Commander and Star Citizen, Richard Garriott created Ultima, and Peter Molyneux created Populous.

questions.question: Which Sony handheld console released in 2004 featured high-end 3D graphics similar to the PS2 and used UMD optical discs?
questions.explanation_correct: The PSP was Nintendo DS's primary rival in the seventh handheld generation, selling over 80 million units.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The PS Vita was PSP's successor in 2011, the Game Boy Advance was Nintendo's handheld, and Gizmondo was a failed multimedia device.

questions.question: Which 1996 action RPG developed by Blizzard North popularized the hack'n'slash genre and online gaming via Battle.net?
questions.explanation_correct: Diablo blended a dark fantasy atmosphere with randomly generated dungeons and a highly addictive loot loop.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nox, Dungeon Siege, and Sacred were early 2000s games inspired by Diablo's success.

questions.question: Which farming RPG was principally developed by Eric Barone and released in 2016?
questions.explanation_correct: Eric Barone created Stardew Valley as an homage to the Harvest Moon series. Its release and later versions also involved publishers and other contributors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Harvest Moon was the primary inspiration, Animal Crossing is by Nintendo, and Terraria is a 2D sandbox platformer.

questions.question: What was the name of the 1972 home console designed by Ralph Baer, recognized as the first home video game system?
questions.explanation_correct: The Magnavox Odyssey displayed simple shapes on a television. Some games used translucent screen overlays supplied with the system.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Atari Pong launched in 1975, Fairchild Channel F introduced cartridges in 1976, and Coleco Telstar was a line of Pong clones.

questions.question: Which 2015 Polish RPG by CD Projekt Red follows Geralt of Rivia in an open-world fantasy adventure?
questions.explanation_correct: The Witcher 3 featured a massive open world, mature storytelling, and acclaimed expansions Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dying Light is a zombie game by Techland, Cyberpunk released in 2020, and Witcher 2 released in 2011.

questions.question: Which Japanese game designer is the mastermind behind the Dark Souls series and serves as president of FromSoftware?
questions.explanation_correct: Miyazaki rose to fame directing Demon's Souls in 2009, creating the 'soulslike' subgenre defined by difficult combat and environmental storytelling.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mikami created Resident Evil, Itsuno directed Devil May Cry games, and Yoko Taro created Nier: Automata.

questions.question: Which 1981 Namco arcade shooter lets a captured player ship be rescued to create a dual fighter?
questions.explanation_correct: In Galaga, a boss Galaga can capture the player’s ship; a rescue can combine two ships into a dual fighter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Frogger is a crossing game, Centipede is a trackball shooter, and Tempest is a vector tube shooter.

questions.question: Which Microsoft console launched in 2005, supported HD output, and competed with the PlayStation 3?
questions.explanation_correct: The Xbox 360 gained massive popularity due to Xbox Live integration and exclusive franchises like Gears of War and Halo 3.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The original Xbox came out in 2001, Xbox One in 2013, and Series X in 2020.

questions.question: Which 2011 independent 2D sandbox game developed by Re-Logic is often referred to as a '2D Minecraft'?
questions.explanation_correct: Terraria focuses on exploration, crafting, building, and fighting powerful bosses in procedurally generated worlds.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Starbound is space-themed, Don't Starve is a survival game, and Rust is a 3D multiplayer survival game.

questions.question: Which id Software co-founder was one of Doom’s designers and designed many of its levels?
questions.explanation_correct: John Romero designed key levels and gameplay mechanics for Doom and Wolfenstein 3D, becoming a prominent industry figure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Carmack was a key programmer, Tom Hall was an id co-founder and designer, and American McGee also designed Doom levels.

questions.question: What was the name of Nintendo's innovative 2006 home console that popularized motion controls with its Wii Remote?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nintendo Wii was a massive commercial hit, attracting casual and family gamers with its intuitive motion controls and Wii Sports.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Wii U was its unsuccessful successor, the Switch is a hybrid console, and the GameCube was Nintendo's classic console.

questions.question: Which 1995/1996 turn-based strategy game developed by New World Computing started the legendary spin-off tactical series?
questions.explanation_correct: The first HoMM game was released in 1995 and its sequel in 1996, paving the way for the legendary Heroes of Might and Magic III in 1999.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Master of Orion is a sci-fi 4X game, Disciples is a gothic rival series, and Age of Wonders combines HoMM and Civ.

questions.question: Which 2018 platformer created by the team led by Maddy Thorson follows Madeline as she climbs a mountain while confronting anxiety?
questions.explanation_correct: Celeste follows Madeline's climb up Celeste Mountain, masterfully blending tight precision platforming with a story of self-acceptance.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Super Meat Boy is a 2010 platformer, Dead Cells is an action roguelite, and Hollow Knight is a metroidvania.

questions.question: Which British game designer is known for inventing the 'god game' genre with titles like Populous and Black & White?
questions.explanation_correct: Molyneux co-founded Bullfrog and Lionhead Studios, known for highly ambitious gameplay ideas and ambitious marketing claims.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sid Meier created Civilization, Will Wright created SimCity/The Sims, and Warren Spector created Deus Ex.

questions.question: Which Nintendo handheld released in 2004 featured two screens, including a touch-sensitive lower screen?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nintendo DS family sold over 154 million units and brought touch-screen and wireless local play to a large audience.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The GBA had a single screen, the 3DS was its 3D successor, and the Switch is a hybrid console.

questions.question: Which space flight simulator by Squad, officially released in 2015 after early-access versions, lets players build rockets and manage a space program?
questions.explanation_correct: Kerbal Space Program uses a simplified physics model based on orbital mechanics to simulate flights of the small green Kerbals.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Elite Dangerous is a space combat sim, SpaceEngine is a 3D universe planetarium, and No Man's Sky is a procedural exploration sandbox.

questions.question: Which atmospheric 2017 metroidvania developed by Team Cherry follows a silent knight exploring the insect kingdom of Hallownest?
questions.explanation_correct: Hollow Knight is highly acclaimed for its hand-drawn art style, difficult boss fights, and vast interconnected world.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ori is a platformer by Moon Studios, Dead Cells is a roguelite, and Shovel Knight is an 8-bit retro platformer.

questions.question: Which 2001 Nintendo home console used proprietary 8 cm optical game discs?
questions.explanation_correct: The GameCube used proprietary 8 cm optical discs. Later Nintendo systems also used proprietary optical formats, generally with larger discs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Nintendo 64 and Super Nintendo used cartridges, while Wii discs were larger.

questions.question: Which 2015 indie RPG created by Toby Fox gained a massive cult following for allowing players to complete the game without killing any enemies?
questions.explanation_correct: Undertale featured unique bullet-hell combat mechanics and a story that adjusted drastically based on the player's choices.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lisa is a dark post-apocalyptic RPG, Deltarune is Fox's follow-up project, and EarthBound is the SNES RPG that inspired it.

questions.question: Which tactical multiplayer shooter debuted in 1999 as a free mod for Half-Life before becoming a premier e-sports FPS franchise?
questions.explanation_correct: Created by Minh Le and Jess Cliffe, Counter-Strike was officially purchased by Valve and released as a standalone game in 2000.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Team Fortress Classic and Day of Defeat are also Half-Life-based games; Unreal Tournament was an arena shooter from Epic Games.

questions.question: Which 1980 Atari arcade game was a first-person 3D tank simulator using vector graphics and a dual-joystick cabinet with a periscope viewer?
questions.explanation_correct: Battlezone was a pioneer in first-person 3D gameplay. A modified version was used by the US military to train infantry fighting vehicle crews.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Star Wars and Red Baron were later vector arcade games, and Armor Attack was a top-down vector game.

questions.question: Which 16-bit Sega console was known in North America as the Genesis, and in Europe and Japan as the Mega Drive?
questions.explanation_correct: The Mega Drive debuted in the late 1980s, engaging in fierce competition against the Super Nintendo during the console wars.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Master System was an 8-bit system, the Game Gear was a handheld, and the Saturn was Sega's 32-bit console.

questions.question: Which founder of Origin Systems created the Ultima RPG series and traveled to space as a private tourist in 2008?
questions.explanation_correct: Garriott, known to gamers as 'Lord British', laid foundations for both single-player computer RPGs and MMORPGs (Ultima Online).
questions.explanation_incorrect: Spector worked at Origin before creating Deus Ex, Romero co-created Doom, and Roberts created Wing Commander.

questions.question: Which 2020 Greek mythology-themed roguelike won multiple Game of the Year awards for its blend of fast-paced action and narrative depth?
questions.explanation_correct: Hades, developed by Supergiant Games, tells the story of Zagreus trying to escape the Underworld ruled by his father, Hades.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dead Cells, Binding of Isaac, and Rogue Legacy are other landmark roguelikes but released in different years.

questions.question: Which 1989 handheld console by Atari was the first in the world to feature a backlit color LCD screen and a reversible design for left-handed players?
questions.explanation_correct: The Atari Lynx was technologically advanced but suffered from a high price point, bulky design, and short battery life.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Game Gear launched a year later, the Game Boy was monochrome, and the Neo Geo Pocket launched in the late 90s.

questions.question: Which 1999 real-time strategy game developed by Ensemble Studios became an iconic medieval RTS, praised for its historical campaigns?
options: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings
questions.answer: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings
questions.explanation_correct: Age of Empires II offered refined multiplayer balance, iconic campaigns involving historical figures, and lasting community support.
questions.explanation_incorrect: StarCraft is a sci-fi RTS, Empire Earth covered ages from prehistoric to future, and Cossacks focused on the 17th and 18th centuries.

questions.question: Which 1980 arcade game created by Namco featured a yellow circular character eating dots in a maze while avoiding colorful ghosts?
questions.explanation_correct: Pac-Man, designed by Toru Iwatani, became a massive cultural phenomenon and one of the highest-grossing arcade games of all time.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Galaga was a space shooter, Dig Dug was about digging underground, and Pole Position was a racing game.

questions.question: Which Nintendo home console launched in Japan in 1990 under the name Super Famicom?
questions.explanation_correct: The SNES featured excellent sound chips and Mode 7 pseudo-3D capabilities, hosting classics like Super Mario World.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The NES was an 8-bit console, the N64 was a 64-bit console released in 1996, and the Virtual Boy was a failed 3D system.

questions.question: Which Canadian writer was lead writer on Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and the first two Mass Effect games?
questions.explanation_correct: Drew Karpyshyn was lead writer on Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect, and co-lead writer with Mac Walters on Mass Effect 2.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hudson directed Mass Effect, Gaider wrote for Dragon Age, and Muzyka co-founded BioWare.

questions.question: Which 2000 action RPG developed by Ion Storm blended FPS, RPG, and stealth elements in a dystopian world of global conspiracies?
questions.explanation_correct: Deus Ex, directed by Warren Spector, gave players unparalleled freedom to choose how to bypass obstacles and complete objectives.
questions.explanation_incorrect: System Shock 2 was developed by Irrational Games and Looking Glass Studios, Thief by Looking Glass, and Half-Life by Valve.

questions.question: Which minimalist 2013 puzzle game created by Lucas Pope casts the player as a border control inspector in the fictional communist state of Arstotzka?
questions.explanation_correct: Papers, Please challenges players with moral dilemmas surrounding survival, family, and obedience to a totalitarian regime.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Obra Dinn was Pope's later game, This War of Mine follows civilians in a war, and Orwell is about digital surveillance.

questions.question: In which year did the PlayStation 2 launch in Japan, going on to become the best-selling home console of all time?
questions.explanation_correct: The PlayStation 2 launched on March 4, 2000, in Japan, eventually selling over 155 million units worldwide.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Dreamcast launched in 1998, the Xbox and GameCube in 2001, and the PSP in 2004.

questions.question: Which 1982 arcade game by Williams Electronics was notable for using two joysticks simultaneously (one for movement, one for shooting)?
questions.explanation_correct: Robotron: 2084, designed by Eugene Jarvis, popularized the twin-stick shooter control scheme in arcade cabinets.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Defender had traditional controls and scrolled horizontally, Joust involved ostrich jousting, and Sinistar featured digitized voice warnings.

questions.question: Which 1994 strategy game developed by Mythos Games and published by MicroProse combined managing an anti-alien organization with turn-based tactical missions?
questions.explanation_correct: Julian Gollop and Mythos Games developed UFO: Enemy Unknown, released as X-COM: UFO Defense in the United States.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Apocalypse was the 1997 third entry, Syndicate was a real-time tactical game, and Jagged Alliance featured turn-based mercenaries.

questions.question: Who was the lead programmer behind the breakthrough 3D graphics engines of Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, and Quake?
questions.explanation_correct: John Carmack, co-founder of id Software, pioneered fast 3D graphics algorithms that defined PC gaming in the 90s.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Abrash worked with Carmack on Quake, Silverman wrote the Build engine, and Sweeney created the Unreal engine.

questions.question: Which 2019 exploration game developed by Mobius Digital tasks players with solving the mystery of a solar system stuck in a 22-minute time loop?
questions.explanation_correct: Outer Wilds was highly praised for its unique sandbox exploration driven entirely by player knowledge and curiosity.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Outer Worlds is an Obsidian RPG, Subnautica is an underwater survival game, and No Man's Sky is a procedural space game.

questions.question: Which Atari home console released in 1993 was marketed as the first 64-bit home console, but failed commercially?
questions.explanation_correct: The Atari Jaguar utilized a complex multi-chip architecture that made programming extremely difficult for third-party developers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Lynx was a handheld, the 5200 was an 8-bit console from the 80s, and the Channel F was from 1976.

questions.question: Which 1990 point-and-click adventure game created by Ron Gilbert for Lucasfilm Games introduced the pirate protagonist Guybrush Threepwood?
questions.explanation_correct: The Secret of Monkey Island was famous for its witty humor, insult sword fighting, and puzzle design.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Loom utilized musical drafts, Maniac Mansion was Gilbert's earlier game, and Full Throttle followed a biker protagonist.

questions.question: Which 2014 Polish survival game developed by 11 bit studios presents a fictional war zone from the perspective of civilians trying to survive?
questions.explanation_correct: This War of Mine was inspired partly by the Siege of Sarajevo. Poland later included the game as supplementary reading for eligible secondary-school students.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Frostpunk is a frozen city-builder survival game, Dead Island is an action zombie game, and Green Hell is set in the Amazon.

questions.question: Who designed the influential 1989 city-building simulation SimCity?
questions.explanation_correct: Will Wright conceived SimCity while developing a map editor for his previous helicopter action game, Raid on Bungeling Bay.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sid Meier created Civilization, Molyneux created Populous, and Romero designed Doom.

questions.question: Which Japanese handheld console released by SNK in 1998 was famous for its micro-switch thumbstick that had an audible click?
questions.explanation_correct: The Neo Geo Pocket and Neo Geo Pocket Color used a small microswitch-based directional stick with an audible click.
questions.explanation_incorrect: WonderSwan was a Bandai handheld, the Game Boy was by Nintendo, and the TurboExpress played TurboGrafx-16 cards.

questions.question: Which 1995 real-time strategy game developed by Westwood Studios kicked off the franchise focusing on the war between the GDI and Nod over Tiberium?
questions.explanation_correct: Command & Conquer (often called Tiberian Dawn) popularized full-motion video (FMV) cutscenes starring real actors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Red Alert was an alternate-history spin-off, Dune II was the genre progenitor, and Warcraft was Blizzard's fantasy RTS.

questions.question: Which 2010 indie puzzle platformer developed by Playdead featured a striking silhouette-style monochrome art design and no text?
questions.explanation_correct: Limbo tells the story of a boy searching for his sister in a dangerous world, utilizing minimal sound design and heavy shadows.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Inside was Playdead's 2016 follow-up, Braid deals with time control, and Fez revolves around 2D/3D perspective shift.

questions.question: Which 1979 Atari arcade game used vector graphics to let players shoot asteroids and flying saucers while managing ship momentum?
questions.explanation_correct: Asteroids was a massive commercial hit for Atari, featuring inertia-based navigation in screen-wrapped space.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lunar Lander was about soft landing, Tempest was a vector tube shooter, and Space Invaders used raster graphics.

questions.question: Which 1990 SNK home console was based on Neo Geo arcade hardware and used large game cartridges?
questions.explanation_correct: The Neo Geo Advanced Entertainment System (AES) was the home console version of the MVS arcade system, using massive cartridges.
questions.explanation_incorrect: PC Engine was NEC's console, Sega Genesis was the 16-bit console, and the 3DO was a 1993 CD platform.

questions.question: Which Valve co-founder worked on the first two releases of Windows before helping found Valve in 1996?
questions.explanation_correct: Gabe Newell worked at Microsoft for 13 years, including managing the first two releases of Windows, before co-founding Valve with Mike Harrington.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mike Harrington also worked at Microsoft and co-founded Valve; the question identifies Newell through his Windows management role. Sweeney founded Epic and Williams co-founded Sierra.

questions.question: Which 2004 game developed by id Software was a horror-focused reboot of the franchise utilizing dynamic lighting and shadow effects?
questions.explanation_correct: Doom 3 utilized the id Tech 4 engine, forcing players to choose between holding a flashlight or a weapon in dark corridors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Quake 4 was released in 2005 on the same engine, while Half-Life 2 and Far Cry focused on outdoor physics and open spaces.

questions.question: Which 2016 cooperative cooking game developed by Ghost Town Games became a highly popular party game focused on chaotic kitchens?
questions.explanation_correct: Overcooked requires tight cooperative multitasking as players prepare meals under strange, moving kitchen layouts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cooking Simulator is a first-person simulation, Chef Life is a restaurant manager, and Keep Talking is about bomb defusal.

questions.question: Which 2012 home console succeeded the Wii and introduced a tablet-like GamePad controller but became a major sales failure?
questions.explanation_correct: The Wii U sold only 13.5 million units due to confusing marketing and a lack of sustained third-party support.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Switch was its highly successful hybrid successor, while the PS4 and Xbox One were standard eighth-generation consoles.

questions.question: Which 1997 real-time strategy game developed by Cavedog Entertainment featured fully 3D terrain and a symphonic orchestral soundtrack?
questions.explanation_correct: Designed by Chris Taylor, the game introduced 3D projectile physics and massive robot battles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: StarCraft was a 2D RTS released in 1998, while Dark Reign and Outlive were lesser-known contemporary strategies.

questions.question: Which 2016 Polish FPS uses the slogan “time moves only when you move” and greatly slows time when the player stands still?
questions.explanation_correct: SUPERHOT began as a game-jam prototype. Time continues very slowly while the player stands still and speeds up when they move.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ruiner is an isometric cyberpunk brawler, Ghostrunner is a first-person cyberpunk slasher, and Bulletstorm is an AAA FPS by People Can Fly.

questions.question: Which American designer created the 1980 mystery game Mystery House and co-founded Sierra On-Line with her husband?
questions.explanation_correct: Roberta Williams designed the pioneering King's Quest series, becoming one of the most influential women in game development.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Jane Jensen created Gabriel Knight, Lori Ann Cole created Quest for Glory, and Amy Hennig wrote Legacy of Kain and Uncharted.

questions.question: Which 8-bit Sega console released in the 1980s was the NES's primary rival, achieving lasting popularity in Brazil?
questions.explanation_correct: The Master System had enduring success in Brazil and sold well in several European markets, although its position varied by region.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Genesis was a 16-bit console, the Saturn was 32-bit, and the SG-1000 was Sega's first home console in 1983.

questions.question: Which 1998 RPG developed by BioWare on the Infinity Engine took players to the Forgotten Realms setting of Dungeons & Dragons?
questions.explanation_correct: Baldur's Gate revived the computer RPG genre with its isometric view, active pause combat, and rich storyline.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Icewind Dale and Planescape were later Infinity Engine games, and Neverwinter Nights used the 3D Aurora Engine.

questions.question: Which 2012 puzzle platformer designed by Phil Fish allowed players to rotate a 2D world to reveal a 3D perspective?
questions.explanation_correct: Fez features the character Gomez in a world he believes is 2D, until he acquires a fez that allows him to shift the perspective in 3D.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Braid is time-based, Super Meat Boy is a high-speed precision platformer, and Spelunky is a platformer roguelike.

questions.question: Which 1981 arcade game created by Nintendo was Shigeru Miyamoto's directorial debut and introduced a giant gorilla?
questions.explanation_correct: Donkey Kong was a major success, establishing Nintendo's presence in the lucrative North American arcade market.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mario Bros. debuted in 1983, Popeye in 1982, and Radar Scope was Nintendo's failed 1979 shooter that Donkey Kong replaced.

questions.question: What is the name of the 2017 hybrid console by Nintendo that can be docked as a home system or used as a handheld?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nintendo Switch became a major commercial success, supported by software like Breath of the Wild.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Wii U was its home-console predecessor, the 3DS was a dedicated handheld, and Nvidia Shield is a family of Android-based devices.

questions.question: Which designer created the 1993 supernatural adventure game Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Fathers?
questions.explanation_correct: Jane Jensen directed the Gabriel Knight series for Sierra, known for its adult tone, rich plot, and voice acting by Tim Curry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Williams created King's Quest, Cole designed Quest for Glory, and Hennig wrote Uncharted.

questions.question: Which 1996 FPS developed by 3D Realms was famous for its interactive environments, humor, and a movie-quoting action hero?
questions.explanation_correct: Duke Nukem 3D utilized Ken Silverman's Build engine, competing directly against id Software's fully 3D Quake.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Quake had a dark, gothic tone, while Blood and Shadow Warrior were other Build engine games.

questions.question: Which 2012 independent space simulation game developed by Subset Games tasks players with managing a ship crew escaping a rebel fleet?
questions.explanation_correct: FTL combined real-time ship management with roguelike randomness and permanent crew death.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Into the Breach was their next game (a turn-based mech strategy), and Crying Suns and Out There were later games inspired by FTL.

questions.question: Which home console released in 1993, manufactured by companies like Panasonic, GoldStar, and Sanyo, failed due to its high $700 launch price?
questions.explanation_correct: The 3DO platform was designed by Trip Hawkins to be licensed by manufacturers, but its $700 price point kept it a niche luxury item.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The CD-i was by Philips, Sega CD was a Genesis add-on, and CD32 was by Commodore.

questions.question: Which 1994 Star Wars space combat game published by LucasArts let players fly Imperial starfighters?
questions.explanation_correct: Developed by Totally Games and published by LucasArts, Star Wars: TIE Fighter followed X-Wing and put players in Imperial cockpits.
questions.explanation_incorrect: X-Wing was the Rebel alliance predecessor, Wing Commander was by Origin, and Rebel Assault was a rail shooter.

questions.question: Which 2018 underwater survival game developed by Unknown Worlds Entertainment requires players to survive on an alien ocean planet?
questions.explanation_correct: Subnautica combined base-building mechanics with underwater exploration, where players avoid colossal Leviathan creatures.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Abzû is an artistic diving game without survival, SOMA is a sci-fi horror game, and Barotrauma is a submarine simulator.

questions.question: Which Williams Electronics arcade game, released in the early 1980s, featured horizontal scrolling and required players to rescue humans from alien abductors?
questions.explanation_correct: Defender required players to coordinate a joystick and five buttons, becoming one of the most profitable arcade games of its era.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Scramble was Konami's side-scroller, Galaxian was a fixed screen shooter, and Vanguard was an early multi-directional shooter.

questions.question: Which Microsoft home console released in late 2001 introduced an internal hard drive and a built-in Ethernet port for online gaming?
questions.explanation_correct: The first Xbox found success primarily in North America, bolstered by Halo: Combat Evolved and the Xbox Live service in 2002.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Xbox 360 was its successor in 2005, while PS2 and GameCube did not feature standard hard drives.

questions.question: Which co-founder of BioWare, a medical doctor by training, led the studio during the development of Baldur's Gate and Mass Effect?
questions.explanation_correct: Ray Muzyka and Greg Zeschuk gave up practicing medicine to form BioWare in 1995 in Edmonton, Canada.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Karpyshyn and Gaider were writers, and Oster was an early programmer who founded Beamdog.

questions.question: Which 2004 Polish FPS developed by People Can Fly was praised for its fast-paced gameplay and original stake gun?
questions.explanation_correct: Painkiller featured fast shooter action against hordes of demons; its arsenal included both the Painkiller and the Stake Gun, two distinct weapons.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bulletstorm was the studio's later 2011 game, Gorky 17 was a tactical RPG, and Call of Juarez was a western by Techland.

questions.question: Which 2015 minimalist strategy game by Thomas van den Berg and collaborators asks players to defend a kingdom and recruit subjects using coins?
questions.explanation_correct: Kingdom was developed by Thomas van den Berg and Marco Bancale, with publisher support; Kingdom: Classic uses side-scrolling art and a simple coin economy.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bad North is a Viking RTS, Thronefall is a 3D minimalist defense game, and Terraria is a sandbox platformer.
